correctness.rationale: For every integer m>=2, the infinite 2 continued-fraction tail evaluates to gamma=1/2-1/[2(2m+1+sqrt2)] and hence h=pi/[2(2m+1+sqrt2)], R=csc h, A=(4pi/3)cot^3 h. The source admissibility threshold A>8 omega3 follows from h<pi/8. Recurrence gives odd q2=2m+1,q3=2m+3,q4=6m+7 and all later q odd. Source Theorem 14(a)/(21), with j0=3 and tail digits two, requires lhs 4pi/[cos(pi/q3)*sqrt(R^2 cos^2(pi/q4)-1)]<=q3; uniform bounds h<1/4,q3>=7,q4>=19 imply lhs<160pi/133<4<q3, so every k>=m+2 is covered. For 2<=k<=m+1, direct odd-multiple distances are strictly decreasing; substitution into source F± gives Fminus=asin(sin h/sin((2k-1)h))-h and Fplus=h-asin(tan h sin(2(k-1)h)). For k<=m the minus condition is exactly 3sin h<sin((4k-1)h), proved by sine concavity on [7h, pi-(3+2sqrt2)h] with the uniform h<1/4 bounds; plus follows from Fplus<h<delta(k+1). At k=m+1, the two strict inequalities reduce to the explicit positive sine combination and sin 2h>tan(sqrt2 h), which hold for h<1/4. Thus source Definition 8 applies to every m, and Theorem 9 gives stated ball rigidity. h~pi/(4m) proves unbounded increasing A~256m^3/(3pi^2). Independent symbolic CF and rational-bound checks and 59,501 direct source-G/F finite comparisons per branch corroborate but do not replace the unlimited theorem.
